memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not have sexual relations with the sister of either your mother or your father, for that would dishonour a close relative; both of you would be held responsible. If a man has sexual relations with his aunt, he has dishonoured his uncle. They will be held responsible; they will die childless.'" - Lev 20:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They will die childless. That phrase carries enormous weight in a culture where children were your future, your name, your security in old age.

The point is not that God arbitrarily withholds children — Scripture elsewhere shows God giving children to the barren and treating childlessness with great tenderness. The point here is that sin has consequences that outlive the moment.

We rarely think that far ahead. Sin promises a present benefit and never mentions the invoice. It offers pleasure now and sends the bill to a future we cannot yet see — to a marriage, to children, to a reputation, to a capacity for trust.

Paul states the principle plainly: Do not be deceived: God cannot be mocked. A man reaps what he sows (Gal 6:7). Note the warning at the front — do not be deceived. He assumes we will try to convince ourselves otherwise.

But he does not stop there. Whoever sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life (Gal 6:8). The principle runs both ways. Faithfulness also compounds. Quiet obedience today produces a harvest years from now that you cannot yet imagine.

What are you sowing this week?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you thought about where your current choices lead in ten years?
2. What are you sowing at the moment, honestly?
3. What faithful thing could you plant today whose harvest comes later?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from short-sighted choices that mortgage my future. Help me sow faithfulness today and trust You with the harvest. Amen.
